messages:
Lucy: heads up — customer report: pagination stalls intermittently when a short-lived API key expires mid-stream. behavior: paginator prefetches pages, many 401s happen, SDK spins up concurrent token refreshes and we hit concurrency limit.

Ben: oof. is the refresh path acquiring the same semaphore as normal requests? that would deadlock.

Lucy: quick snippet of how they call it:

```
const it = client.listBlobs.paginate({ pageSize: 50, prefetch: 3 });
for await (const page of it) { process(page.items); }
```

They use default concurrency cap of 10. When token expires the first request gets 401, triggers `auth.refresh()` which does an HTTP call. Meanwhile prefetch keeps firing and we run out of sem permits.

Raj: do we dedupe refreshes? i.e., singleflight so only one refresh happens and others wait for result?

Lucy: nope — current JS SDK doesn't have singleflight. every 401 triggers a new refresh call and each refresh attempt itself acquires the same concurrency token because refresh is treated like any outbound request. so lots of refreshes + pending page requests = semaphore saturation.

Tina: interesting. py sdk uses a refresh lock and doesn't count refresh calls against `maxConcurrency`, IIRC. SDK parity gap.

Ben: immediate workarounds for customers?

Lucy: recommend set `prefetch: 0` and set `maxConcurrency: 3` for now. We can also advise short token rotation window avoid mid-stream expirations.

Raj: long term fixes:
- separate auth/refresh path from regular request concurrency (don't acquire page semaphore for refresh)
- implement refresh singleflight/deduper so only one network call runs per expired token
- add preemptive refresh before starting paginator when token TTL < threshold
- make prefetch opt-in and document interaction with auth/refresh and concurrency

Tina: also add telemetry: count "concurrent-refreshes" and emit a diag when >1 refresh in-flight for same account. that'll help hosted customers.

Ben: good call. can we also change default so prefetch=1 instead of 3? or 0?

Raj: maybe 1 is safer. But SDK parity note — py uses prefetch=1. make JS match.

Lucy: I'll open an issue with reproduction steps + a mocked token expiry test. attaching log excerpt:

```
[09:14:02] page 1 fetched
[09:14:05] resp 401 id=xyz token-expired
[09:14:05] refresh start id=xyz-r1
[09:14:05] refresh start id=xyz-r2
[09:14:06] semaphore held=10
[09:14:07] refresh resp 200 r1
[09:14:07] page 2 request started
[09:14:15] semaphore held=10
```

Ben: assign to @raj for the auth flow changes. Add tests: singleflight, ensure refresh doesn't consume page semaphore, and ensure paginator prefetch behavior doesn't oversubscribe.

Tina: docs: quickstart note about token lifetime and pagination + example how to prewarm token: `await client.auth.ensureFresh()` before long paginated jobs.

Lucy: thanks — I'll include that snippet in the issue. also pinging infra for telemetry metric.

devex-bot: Created issue #1499: "JS paginator + token refresh thundering herd causing concurrency saturation". CI job: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/1499-token-refresh-repro

Raj: plan: reproducible test this afternoon, patch will: (1) add refresh dedupe, (2) decouple refresh from page semaphore, (3) change default prefetch to 1, publish patch 1.4.0-rc.1

Ben: make sure to add an integration test that simulates TTL expiry mid-iteration so we don't regress.

Lucy: ok, will update issue with failing test. will notify the customer once we have a patch. :pray: 

Tina: small follow-up — maybe add a "maxRefreshConcurrency" config so customers can throttle refreshes if needed.

Raj: noted. closing loop after PR lands.
